references.text: The psalmist affirms that the Lord's word stands firm in heaven forever, and his faithfulness endures from generation to generation. Heaven and earth are established and endure according to God's decrees. This underscores the eternal validity of the law, which Jesus speaks about in [ref:Sal 119:89-91|Psalm 119:89-91].

Isaiah proclaims that the grass withers and the flower fades, but God's word stands firm forever ([ref:Jes 40:8|Isaiah 40:8]). This parallels Jesus' statement that it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one tiny letter of the law to disappear.

Isaiah says that the heavens will vanish like smoke and the earth will grow old like a garment, but God's salvation endures forever and his righteousness will not fail ([ref:Jes 51:6|Isaiah 51:6]). God's law and his word surpass even the permanence of heaven and earth.

In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus says he has not come to abolish the Law or the Prophets but to fulfill them. Not one tiny letter or stroke will disappear from the Law until everything has happened ([ref:Matt 5:17-18|Matthew 5:17-18]). This is the closest parallel to Luke 16:17 and expresses the same truth about the unchangeable nature of the law.

Jesus says that heaven and earth will pass away, but his words will never pass away ([ref:Matt 24:35|Matthew 24:35]). Jesus' words and God's law have a permanence that surpasses even the created world.

Also in Mark's version of the end-times discourse, Jesus confirms that heaven and earth will pass away, but his words will never pass away ([ref:Mark 13:31|Mark 13:31]). This supports the principle of the eternal validity of God's word.

In Luke's version of Jesus' end-times speech, the same is repeated: Heaven and earth will pass away, but Jesus' words will never pass away ([ref:Luk 21:33|Luke 21:33]). Once again, the unchangeable nature of the law and God's word is confirmed.

Peter quotes Isaiah and states that the Lord's word stands forever ([ref:1 Pet 1:25|1 Peter 1:25]). This is the gospel preached to the readers, confirming the eternal and unshakable nature of God's word and law.

Paul asks whether we then nullify the Law by faith, and answers: By no means! We uphold the Law ([ref:Rom 3:31|Romans 3:31]). This aligns with Jesus' words that the Law will not disappear but be upheld.
